purpose: Independent practice of B1.1 (decomposition) and B1.2 (comparison). Captures formative evidence on flexibility and place-value reasoning.
student_learning_goal: I can compose and decompose numbers to 200 in different ways, and compare numbers using place-value reasoning.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can compose and decompose numbers to 200 in different ways, and compare numbers using place-value reasoning.
header.character_watermark: Detective Tina Tens in the top-right corner with a striped vest and magnifying glass. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Each box has a target number. Write THREE different decompositions for the number.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Three target-number boxes stacked vertically. Each box ~7in × 1.5in. Format per box: target number on the left in a circle (89, 132, 178), three decomposition lines on the right.

image_placeholders.description: Three target-number boxes in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each box ~7in × 1.5in. Left side: a circle ~1.2in across with the target number. Right side: three blank decomposition lines '___ + ___ + ___ = 89' etc. Targets: T1=89, T2=132, T3=178.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; three boxes stacked.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P1_THREE_TARGETS: keywords (target, decomposition) name what the boxes ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Write > or < between each pair. Then write 1 line saying WHY using the place-value rule.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Six comparison rows. Each row shows two numbers with a blank in the middle for the symbol, plus a 'Why?' reason line.

image_placeholders.description: Six comparison rows in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each row ~7in × 0.7in. Number boxes on each side, > / < bubbles in the middle for selection, a 'Why?' line below. Pairs: 147 vs 174, 89 vs 102, 134 vs 143, 178 vs 187, 99 vs 100, 156 vs 165.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; six rows.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P2_SIX_COMPARES: keywords (compare, place-value) name what the rows ask for.

parts.answer_key: 147 < 174 (same hundreds, 4 tens vs 7 tens). 89 < 102 (0 hundreds vs 1 hundred). 134 < 143 (same hundreds, 3 vs 4 tens). 178 < 187 (same hundreds, 7 vs 8 tens). 99 < 100 (0 hundreds vs 1 hundred). 156 < 165 (same hundreds, 5 vs 6 tens).

parts.student_instructions: Order these numbers from SMALLEST to BIGGEST. Write them in the boxes in order.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. Five number cards on the left (67, 134, 89, 178, 145) and five empty ordering boxes on the right with arrows.

image_placeholders.description: An ordering layout in B&W line-art, ~7in × 2.5in. Left side: 5 number cards in random order (67, 134, 89, 178, 145). Right side: 5 empty boxes in a row with right-arrows between them, labeled 'smallest to biggest'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P3_ORDER: keywords (order, smallest, biggest) name what the layout asks for.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over. Pick a number between 100 and 200. Write FIVE different decompositions of it.
teacher_notes: Lesson 2 consolidation. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Use Part 1 as evidence of B1.1 decomposition flexibility — children writing only 3 standard splits are at L3; children producing creative non-standard splits are at L4. Use Part 2's 89-vs-102 row as the strongest test of place-value reasoning — children who pick 89 are still applying ones-first reasoning.
